subject: Pricing: proposed surge-protocol and variable-floor ladder
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmehealth.com>, Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pricing: proposed surge-protocol and variable-floor ladder

Hi Jordan / Samira—

Thanks again for the time last week. As promised, attached is a short playbook that describes the compromise we discussed on the call: a four-quarter variable-floor ladder combined with a surge-protocol that triggers temporary floor relief when monthly consumption spikes due to go-live events. The purpose is to protect Acme against anomalous onboarding spikes while keeping the long-term minimum economics intact for both sides.

Key points in the attached pricing_playbook_v0.3.docx (attached):
- Variable floor ladder: 3 tiers over the first 12 months (baseline, step-up, stabilized).
- Surge protocol: temporary 60-day floor relief window when usage exceeds 3x baseline and Customer provides a go-live notice.
- Billing: monthly invoicing with quarterly true-up and annual true-up for any shortfall vs. committed band.
- Ops/Implementation: Redwood will provide an operations mapping sheet (OrderForm_edited_for_ops.xlsx) that shows how surge windows map to autoscale/burst credits.

Ask from Acme: please have your legal team mark up the order form with any redlines on the floor/cap language and highlight operational concerns (billing cadence, reporting hooks, audit logs). If the surge window is acceptable we can draft specific language to slot in Exhibit A (pricing schedule) rather than broad contract language.

Proposed near-term path:
1) You send a redline against the Order Form (we'll accept PDF annotations) — ideal by end of day Thursday.
2) If material, Redwood legal (Laura) will propose tracked edits; ops (Karthik) will quantify any burst credit exposure.
3) Finalize commercial terms and push to DocuSign for signature.

FYI attaching the playbook as a working doc. Let me know if you'd prefer the surge window to be event-driven or metric-only.

Thanks,
Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts (Americas)
Redwood Inference
attachments: pricing_playbook_v0.3.docx (docx)
From: Jordan Price <jordan.price@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samira Khan <samira.khan@acmehealth.com>, Acme Health Legal <legal@acmehealth.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Mar 2028 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing: proposed surge-protocol and variable-floor ladder

Marissa—

Thanks for the doc. Attached is a marked-up redline of the Order Form (ACME_OrderForm_redline_v1.pdf). A few quick items from our side:

1) Minimum commit / floor: the current floor in Exhibit A still reads as an annual hard minimum that would be applied pro rata monthly. That exposes us if a one-month onboarding spike happens and then usage drops — we need either (a) a monthly cap on how much of the annual floor can be reallocated to a single month, or (b) an explicit carve-out for go-live surge months where the month is excluded from minimum calculations if pre-notified.

2) Billing / true-up cadence: we prefer a monthly invoicing with 30-day adjustments rather than quarterly true-ups. The reason is constrained internal chargeback cycles. Would Redwood accept monthly true-ups for any months within the surge window and keep annual reconciliation for anything outside?

3) Burst credits: your playbook mentions autoscale/burst credits but the order form does not detail how credits are applied or their expiry. We need an operational table showing credit accrual and expiry.

I've highlighted those sections in the PDF and added alternative language for the surge carve-out. Also looping in legal — they may have more redlines.

Can we aim to get a draft that Laura can sign off on by next Tuesday?

Regards,
Jordan Price
Director, Cloud Platforms
Acme Health
attachments: ACME_OrderForm_redline_v1.pdf (pdf)

Subject: Re: Pricing: proposed surge-protocol and variable-floor ladder — suggested language + ops workbook

Marissa / Laura —

I reviewed ACME's redline and sketched a compromise we can take to them. Attaching an ops workbook (OrderForm_edited_for_ops.xlsx) that maps: baseline tiers -> burst credit buckets -> expiry windows. Key recommended commercial positions:

- Trade position on floor: accept a go-live carve-out that excludes up to two surge months per 12-month period from floor calculations, provided Acme gives 7 days’ notice and identifies the event (go-live / marketing push).
- Monthly true-up concession: accept monthly true-ups during a declared surge window only. Outside surge windows, continue with quarterly true-ups and annual reconciliation.
- Cap exposure guardrail: add a clause that net liability from surge relief is limited to X% of the annual committed value (ops to provide exact percent in workbook).
- Burst credit mechanics: credits accrue at time of overage, expire after 90 days, and can be used against incremental usage only (not to satisfy floors).
- Audit & reporting: Redwood will provide a surge report within 10 business days of a request showing metric history, KV cache usage, and billing line items.

If Laura's legal team is comfortable with tracked language I drafted below, we can send a consolidated tracked edit for ACME to review. If not, we should propose specific alternate text.

Draft language (high level, placeholder to be converted to tracked edits):
"Surge Carve-Out: Customer may designate up to two (2) Surge Months in each 12‑month period by providing Redwood with at least seven (7) days’ prior written notice. For designated Surge Months, usage associated with the designated event shall be excluded from calculations of the Annual Minimum Commitment. Surges outside of this notice window will be reviewed in good faith and may be considered on a case-by-case basis."

Operational follow-ups for Laura / Ops:
- Laura: can you map the above draft into Exhibit A language (tracked edits)?
- Ops (Marissa / Karthik): provide the percent exposure cap and the mechanics cell in the workbook before we send the consolidated redline.

Happy to jump on a 30 min call with Acme if they prefer to walk the redline live.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Sales — Americas
Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 08 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pricing: proposed surge-protocol and variable-floor ladder — consolidated next steps

Jordan / Samira —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for the detailed redline. Per Karthik's note above and Laura's inline comments (see consolidated edits attached), here's the path forward I propose so we can close this commercial quickly: 

1) Surge carve-out: Redwood will accept the "two Surge Months per 12-month period with 7 days’ notice" approach. We will convert Karthik's draft into tracked edits in Exhibit A and send the consolidated order form back to Acme for one more pass.

2) Monthly true-ups during surge: agreed — during a declared Surge Month we will calculate true-ups monthly. For months outside declared surges, we will revert to quarterly true-ups with annual reconciliation.

3) Cap exposure guardrail: ops recommends setting a cap of 15% of the annual committed value as the maximum net liability Redwood would carry from surge relief. Karthik will confirm the percent in the workbook; currently we have a working value of 15%.

4) Burst credits: Redwood confirms accrual at overage; credits expire after 90 days and cannot be used to satisfy Annual Minimums. We'll add the table from OrderForm_edited_for_ops.xlsx to Exhibit A.

Next actions:
- We will produce a consolidated tracked-edit Order Form (ACME_OrderForm_consolidated_v2.pdf) by EOD Friday.
- If that looks good, Marissa will send the DocuSign envelope with Exhibit A and the Order Form for signature.

Please reply with any outstanding legal concerns; if none, we'll proceed on the timeline above. Happy to set up a 30-minute sync if you want to walk the final doc line-by-line.

Best,
Marissa
Head of Strategic Accounts (Americas)
Redwood Inference
